description: Brassica oleracea var. capitata: a head of tightly wrapped leaves.

diseases.name: Alternaria Leaf Spot
diseases.description: A fungal leaf spot of cabbage and other brassicas with dark, target-like spots.
diseases.causes: Spores survive on brassica debris and seed and spread by wind and rain in warm, wet weather.
symptoms: Round brown to black spots with concentric rings
A yellow halo round the spots
Dark spots on heads and stems too
diseases.effect: Spotted outer leaves and blemished heads reduce quality.
diseases.untreated: Severe spotting reaches the harvested part.

steps.title: Remove spotted outer leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off spotted outer leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

prevention.title: Rotate away from brassicas for 3 years

lifecycle: The fungus survives on debris and seed.
Wind and rain carry spores to leaves.
Dark ringed spots with halos form.
Spots reach the heads in wet weather.

diseases.name: Black Rot
diseases.description: The most serious bacterial disease of cabbage and other brassicas: V-shaped yellow lesions from the leaf edge with blackened veins.
diseases.causes: Bacteria come in on seed and transplants and spread by rain splash, tools and insects; they enter through the pores at the leaf edge.
symptoms: Yellow, V-shaped lesions from the leaf margin, pointing to the midrib
Veins in the lesions turn black
Lesions brown and dry; the vascular ring in the stem blackens
diseases.effect: Leaves die and heads are stunted and rot.
diseases.untreated: Whole plantings can be lost in warm, wet seasons.

steps.title: Remove infected leaves and plants
steps.instruction: Pick off infected leaves and plants when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer bacteria splash to healthy plants.

steps.title: Do not work in wet crops
steps.instruction: Keep out of the field while leaves are wet and disinfect tools.

steps.title: Plan rotation and clean seed
steps.instruction: Use hot-water-treated seed and rotate 3 years.

lifecycle: Bacteria come in on seed or transplants.
Rain splash carries them to leaf edges.
They enter the veins: yellow V-shaped lesions form.
Veins blacken and the infection moves into the stem.

diseases.name: Downy Mildew
diseases.description: A water-mould disease of cabbage and other brassicas, worst in cool, damp weather.
diseases.causes: Spores spread by wind and splash from infected plants and debris; cool nights with leaf wetness let them infect.
symptoms: Yellow, angular patches on the upper leaf
White to grey downy growth underneath
Patches turn brown; heads may be discoloured inside
diseases.effect: Spotted leaves and heads lose quality.

steps.title: Remove affected leaves
steps.instruction: Pick off affected leaves when the plants are dry and take them away.
steps.rationale: Fewer spores are left to spread.

steps.title: Improve airflow
steps.instruction: Space plants and avoid evening watering.

steps.title: Protective spray
steps.instruction: Spray a registered fungicide on the label's schedule.
steps.rationale: Protects healthy growth; it cannot cure what is already infected.

lifecycle: Spores come from infected plants and debris.
Cool, damp nights let them infect.
Yellow angular patches form, white down underneath.
